title: a sibling born after a parent died
line: a brother an obituary's index names under its own sibling grouping is created by the owner, not the rule, and is not placed as a child of the couple when the mother's accepted death comes before his birth: a half sibling is possible, a placement under her is not

steps.say: the owner's own word on the parents' names and on the mother's death, 30 October 1918

his obituary, the file's own citation, accepted by the owner: his brother Joe Davidson, whom the tree does not hold, stands in the index's own Parents and Siblings table, a grouping the rule creates nobody on

why.has: the record's indexer, not the record, relates them to a person accepted on it (Brother)

expect.why: the index groups him as a brother; the rule creates a person only on a relationship the record states
her name rests on the owner's word: the stated child is one point on a link the file claims, two are needed; the owner decides

steps.say: the owner creates him from the obituary: the parents are not yet accepted on it, so there is no home to place him in
the birth year his Find a Grave index entry gives him (1925), planted: no harness record dates his birth
the parents accepted on the obituary by the owner: the son's place in their family now stands on it
the obituary read again: each decision carries to the new reading, and the placement beside him is examined now

expect.why: no membership in the couple's family: a mother dead seven years before his birth
